text:
CITATION
:
Katz v. Katz, 2010 ONSC 4344

COURT
FILE NO.:
FC-06-23535-00

DATE:
2010-08-05

SUPERIOR COURT OF JUSTICE - ONTARIO

RE:
Orly
Katz, Applicant in person

AND:

Neil Ari Katz, Respondent in
person

BEFORE:
McGee J.

COUNSEL:
S. Westreich for Jewish
Family & Child Services, agent for D. Millstone counsel for Linda Chodos
and Family Solutions

N. Calla for Associated Hebrew
Schools, Jewish Vocational Services (Toronto), and TanenbaumCHAT

HEARD:
August
4, 2010

Endorsement

Background

[
1
]

The Applicant and Respondent are parents of
three sons, Samuel aged 23 is now married, Jordan is 18 and Corey is 11.

[
2
]

The parties separated on a final basis in May of
2004.  The litigation was protracted, confused and expensive.  The May 2009 Trial
proceeded before Justice Hughes, consumed seven days of court time, and a year
of deliberation inclusive of written closing submissions received in November
of 2009.  Final Judgment was released on April 26, 2010.

[
3
]

The Trial Judgment is an exhaustive and detailed
analysis of all the claims arising from the parties’ separation.  The Final
Order has been issued and entered.

[
4
]

On the face of it, today’s proceeding might suggest
that Mr. Katz is simply unhappy with the trial decision.  Since its release he
has brought four basket motions which heap blame and ill-feeling upon the
solicitors, the assessor and the children’s physician.  However, I fear there
is a more concerning dynamic at work, one that would use the court system for
an improper purpose.

[
5
]

Mr. Katz has projected in a rather bizarre manner a
litany of complaints onto the many professionals who have assisted this family
over the period of litigation.  He includes in his motions that the Court make
an order that the Law Society of Upper Canada provide to him certain
undertakings respecting the College of Physicians and Surgeons, and that the
Law Society ensure that family law professionals obtain appropriate training.

[
6
]

The motions were brought to Justice Hughes
attention and she prepared a detailed endorsement on June 16 dismissing the
various relief sought.  In paragraph 6 of that endorsement she reminds Mr. Katz
that these various persons or organizations are not parties to the action and
there is no jurisdiction upon which to make an Order against them.

[
7
]

It appears that Mr. Katz seized upon this
admonition and substituted his own analysis that should the named bodies be
added as parties, Orders could be made.  On Friday July 22, 2010 he fashioned
an “Enforcement Motion” which he then served on Jewish
Family & Child Services, Linda Chodos (the assessor whose recommendations
he agreed with at the commencement of Trial), Associated Hebrew Schools, (where
Corey attends and his mother teaches), Jewish Vocational Services (Toronto,)
and TanenbaumCHAT.  He served everyone on July 23 including Ms. Katz and set
the matter for hearing today, with some seven working days for the various
organizations to respond.

[
8
]

I learned in today’s submissions that Mr. Katz
is also seeking leave to appeal the Final Order of April 26, 2010.

August 4, 2010 Motion

[
9
]

Mr. Katz brings this motion without benefit of an
originating process or case conference.  He does not seek a variation of the
prior Final Order.  Rather, he stated to me in his own words, that his
intention is to hold various organizations and persons accountable to the
children.  Given the ages of the boys, and the finding made by Justice Hughes
in her Judgment, I do not accept that the children have had any part in Mr.
Katz’ imaginings.  This is entirely his initiative, cloaked in the guise of a
child’s best interest, to challenge those who will not do his bidding.

[
10
]

Mr. Katz’ written materials did not entirely match
his oral presentation, but it is useful to note some of the relief sought in
the former:

-that the Associated Hebrew Schools, Linda Chodos and Family Solutions,
Jewish Child and Family Services, TanenbaumCHAT, and JVS Toronto be added to
parties in this proceeding and that they be compelling to provide him with
disclosure, and that they provide to him written explanations pertaining to his
inquiries.

-an order that the Associated Hebrew School, Linda Chodos, Family
Solutions and JF & CS no longer talk amongst themselves with respect to
Corey in order to mitigate against and minimize the conflict that has prevailed
within these proceedings.

-an Order that both JS&CS and Linda Chodos and Family Solutions be
compelled to share with the respondent any information they have on Samuel
[Samuel is 23].

[
11
]

Within his oral submissions Mr. Katz expanded
upon these themes and embarked upon various ramblings, such as the school’s
authority to vaccinate his children and other tangents which I halted given the
severe time constraints on a busy motions list in Newmarket.  He was clear on two
overriding themes: that the various service providers should be made to explain
how they could have formed their conclusions or taken certain actions; and that
the system is broken and must be fixed.

[
12
]

It would not be beyond the scope of human nature
to simply attribute today’s motion to the manifestation of an ill mind.  Although
Mr. Katz states that he is not under the care of a physician, psychologist or
psychiatrist, he is clearly disturbed and unable to move forward in his life.
In contrast, Ms. Katz wisely, and sadly questions when, if ever, this conflict
can be over.  She works hard at her profession as a teacher, earns modest wages
and wants no more than to have this period of her life come to a close.

[
13
]

Counsel have presented me with strong argument
for a dismissal of the motion.  Counsel for Jewish Child and Family Services
provided me with the case of
L. v. L
.
1990 CanLII 12276 (ON CTGD)
, 1990 Carswell Ont 338, 31 R.F.L.
(3
rd
) 320 in which Justice Gautreau determines that a Society shall
not be added as a party to a family law proceeding.  That decision speaks of
the need to avoid fettering the discretion of a Society to act freely and
without fear in matters concerning the protection of children.  She suggests
this is a principle that can be applied to all the respondents to this motion,
and there is much merit in this view.

[
14
]

Service providers, assessors and those who
provide support to families transitioning through a separation must be free to
act without fear of retaliation by an unsuccessful litigant.  Subject to
appeal, a Final Order is a Final Order.  It would bring the administration of
justice into disrepute to permit a disgruntled party to relitigate lost issues
by attacking those who have tendered evidence or services in the course of the
litigation.

[
15
]

In summary, the motion must fail on both a
procedural basis and a substantive analysis.  There is no application before me
in which the relief claimed can be founded, and neither has there been a case
conference per Rule 14(4) of the
Family Law Rules.
On this basis alone
the Motion can be dismissed.  I also find that the relief sought by Mr. Katz is
either outside of the statutory framework, or with respect to adding the named
respondents as parties - wholly without merit.

[
16
]

The Motion is dismissed.

No Motion without Court’s permission

[
17
]

Rule 21 of the
family Law Rules
provides
that:

(21)  If
a party tries to delay the case or add to its costs or in any other way to
abuse the court’s process by making numerous motions without merit, the court
may order the party not to make any other motions in the case without the
court’s permission.
O. Reg. 114/99, r. 14 (21)
.

[
18
]

It is entirely appropriate to make this order in
these circumstances.  This is the respondent’s fifth motion in as many months.
The matter went to Trial in 2009 and a final decision was released on April 26,
2010.  The applicant and the remaining minor child, deserves the court’s
attention to ensure that Mr. Katz be prevented from using the court process for
an improper purpose.  The other respondents to this motion are primarily not
for profit organizations whose limited budgets ought to be focused on
individuals and families in need, not spurious litigation.

[
19
]

Order to go that the respondent, Neil Ari Katz
shall not take any further steps in this proceeding without leave of the court.

Costs

[
20
]

The costs sought by the respondents to this
motion are exceedingly reasonable.  Counsel for Jewish Family & Child
Services seeks an amount of $1,152.60, and as agent for counsel for Linda
Chodos; she seeks the amount of $600.  Counsel for Associated Hebrew Schools,
Jewish Vocational Services and TanenbaumCHAT seeks costs of $915, $610 and $915
respectively.  All counsel have provided me with breakdowns of hourly rates
supporting today’s attendance and preparation.

[
21
]

Ms. Katz indicates that as she is on summer
break, she has not lost income as a result of this motion and does not seek
costs. I would have granted her costs had she so requested.

[
22
]

Order to go granting costs to the respondents as
requested above, to be paid by Mr. Katz forthwith.

Justice H. McGee

Date Released:
August 5, 2010
